result.title: Cognitively Decoupled Meta-Induction for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
result.summary: In-context learning (ICL) tackles downstream tasks conditioned on demonstrations. This paradigm relies heavily on neighbor-based matching between queries and demonstrations, limiting out-of-distribution (OOD) performance. For better generalization, rule-based inductive reasoning derives task-level regularities, which we term task-level inductive representations (TIR), before directly answering. However, existing methods lack generalizable inductive ability across diverse tasks. Inspired by meta-learning, we propose Cognitive-Decoupling meta-Induction (CoDI) for TIR-based inductive reasoning on general tasks. CoDI comprises a Cognitive-Decoupling Framework for query-blind TIR induction, and a Dual-Loop Meta-Inductive Learning method for cross-task inducer optimization. Empirically, CoDI achieves substantial performance gains on five ID and OOD benchmarks, and preserves OOD gains without explicit induction at inference. Code is available at https://github.com/Yuqian-Wang2277/codi-meta-induction.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 CoDI，用元学习构建「认知解耦」框架，先在与查询无关的条件下归纳任务级归纳表示（TIR），再据此直接作答，并以双环元归纳学习实现跨任务的归纳器优化，在五个 ID/OOD 基准上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把任务规律压缩为查询无关的 TIR 并用双环元学习训练归纳器，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的诱导方式、跨任务监督设计以及「线索归纳与作答解耦」提供可供核查的方法线索。虽是纯文本 ICL 工作，但与视觉推理无直接关系。
